answer: Sybil resistance runs on bonded, audited edges, not names. An agent posts collateral, registers a hardware attestation, then must bridge two unrelated subgraphs: the protocol samples a random vertex and asks that agent to co-sign a live challenge with a stranger it never traded with. A puppet farm cannot fake such an edge cheaply, since every clone needs its own stake, its own sealed device, and a thirty-day quiet period before its signatures score at all. One failed audit slashes the whole vine of accounts sharing that operator, so a thousand fake seats cost far more than one honest one.
